name: Baccharis

study_strategy.warning: Many fall composites need comparison by structure, not just bloom color.

look_here_first: Check whether the shrub has alternate narrow leaves and many tiny composite heads; then inspect a head and its phyllaries. For species, compare leaf margins/shape and reproductive heads, not flowering season alone.
shared_traits: Woody or shrubby composites with alternate simple leaves
Numerous small capitula with involucral phyllaries
Male and female flowers usually on separate plants (dioecious)

comparison_matrix.leaf: Usually narrow, small leaves; inspect margins and upper/lower stem positions
comparison_matrix.heads: Compare terminal cluster architecture and phyllary series

comparison_matrix.leaf: Willow-like lanceolate leaves, often serrate; compare mid-stem leaves
comparison_matrix.heads: Check reproductive heads and involucral structure
comparison_matrix.caution: Leaf variation and wet-site habit are supporting, not decisive

overlap_cautions: Leaf width and serration vary by shoot age; compare leaves at matching positions.
Sex of heads differs between individuals; do not treat male-versus-female head differences as species differences.
Habitat alone is not a safe separator.
lookalikes: Pluchea: glandular aromatic herb/subshrub with different head structure
Solidago: typically showier golden composite inflorescences and different head construction
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched mid-stem leaf blades and margins with scale
Same-sex flower-head macro for both species with phyllaries labeled
Whole inflorescence architecture at same growth stage
Male and female head comparison within each species to prevent sex confusion

handoffs.question: Verify reliable phyllary counts, leaf gland and margin thresholds for B. neglecta versus B. salicifolia before adding a hard dichotomous key.
